plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 after two compilation failures: (1) material name truncation ('si' vs 'sio2'), (2) layer count mismatch (declared 19, experiment had 22). Three new routes fix these issues by: (1) explicitly stating exact layer counts in both proposed_topology and execution_request_english, (2) using verified IR dielectric material identifiers from evidence (Ge/ZnS pair from CorpusId:237542117), (3) implementing multi-cavity Fabry-Perot topology with deterministic initialization. All routes maintain parent_route_id='route_02' per refinement_chain instruction.

routes.title: Three-Cavity Fabry-Perot Dual-Band Filter with Ge/ZnS Material Pair
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 3-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter using Ge (high-index) and ZnS (low-index) dielectric materials on CaF2 substrate can achieve simultaneous high transmittance in both 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm bands while maintaining strong blocking in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm ranges, within 24-layer constraint.
routes.design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot design with alternating quarter-wave Bragg reflectors and spacer layers, computationally optimized for dual-band transmission. Evidence from CorpusId:237542117 demonstrates Ge/ZnS pair achieves >83.5% transmittance in mid-IR with OD3 blocking.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [Bragg-HL]_3 | Cavity1-Spacer | [Bragg-HL]_3 | Cavity2-Spacer | [Bragg-HL]_3 | Cavity3-Spacer | [Bragg-HL]_3 | CaF2 substrate. Total finite layers: 21 layers (12 Bragg mirror layers + 3 cavity spacers + 6 coupling layers).
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and ZnS are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
total thickness should remain under 10 μm for stress management
expected_advantages: Ge/ZnS high index contrast reduces required layer count
Evidence demonstrates achievable >83% transmittance in mid-IR
known_risks: Fabrication tolerance may reduce transmittance and increase ripple per evidence
Total thickness may approach stress limits
Dual-band optimization may compromise individual band performance
routes.execution_request_english: Design and optimize a 21-layer dielectric multilayer bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate for dual-band transmission. Stack structure from air incident side: Layer 1-6 (Bragg mirror: Ge/ZnS/Ge/ZnS/Ge/ZnS), Layer 7 (Cavity1 spacer: Ge), Layer 8-13 (Bragg mirror: ZnS/Ge/ZnS/Ge/ZnS/Ge), Layer 14 (Cavity2 spacer: ZnS), Layer 15-20 (Bragg mirror: Ge/ZnS/Ge/ZnS/Ge/ZnS), Layer 21 (Cavity3 spacer: Ge), then CaF2 substrate. All 21 layer thicknesses are optimization variables with bounds: 50 nm to 2000 nm. Optimize for: maximize transmittance in 4150-4350 nm band, maximize transmittance in 4550-4750 nm band, minimize transmittance in 3600-4000 nm band, minimize transmittance in 4850-5200 nm band. Normal incidence, air ambient, CaF2 substrate. Use Ge and ZnS as dielectric materials (no metals). Report best_target_score, valid_candidates count, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Fixes prior compilation failures: (1) explicit 21-layer count stated in both proposed_topology and execution_request_english to prevent mismatch, (2) correct material names Ge and ZnS instead of truncated identifiers, (3) deterministic cavity-based initialization following evidence from CorpusId:237542117.

routes.title: Two-Cavity Fabry-Perot with Reduced Layer Count for Manufacturability
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A simplified 2-cavity Fabry-Perot filter with 17 total layers using Ge/ZnS can achieve acceptable dual-band transmission while improving fabrication tolerance and reducing total thickness compared to 3-cavity design.
routes.design_principle: Reduce cavity count from 3 to 2 to decrease sensitivity to thickness errors while maintaining dual-band capability through careful spacer thickness selection. Evidence suggests bandwidth depends on layer count but transmittance depends on thickness tolerance.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [Bragg-HL]_3 | Cavity1-Spacer | [Bragg-HL]_2 | Cavity2-Spacer | [Bragg-HL]_3 | CaF2 substrate. Total finite layers: 17 layers (12 Bragg mirror layers + 2 cavity spacers + 3 coupling layers).

routes.title: Four-Cavity Fabry-Perot with Maximum Layer Budget for Enhanced Blocking
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 4-cavity Fabry-Perot filter utilizing all 24 available layers with Ge/ZnS can achieve superior stopband blocking (OD>3) while maintaining high dual-band transmittance, leveraging evidence that more layers enable narrower bandwidth and better blocking.
routes.design_principle: Maximize layer count to 24 to exploit evidence that bandwidth narrows and blocking improves with increased layer count. Four cavities provide additional degrees of freedom for dual-band shaping and stopband suppression.
